points.t: A patient on methotrexate, ciclosporin, a biologic or a JAK inhibitor needs a prescription, a vaccine, an antibiotic or advice.
Targeted blockade of TNF, IL-17, IL-23, IL-4/13 or JAK signalling, or broad immunosuppression (methotrexate, ciclosporin).
Specialist-initiated (NICE TAs); shared-care monitoring; no live vaccines on most; check every new drug for interactions (methotrexate + trimethoprim).
Serious infection, TB reactivation, methotrexate toxicity (mouth ulcers, cytopenia), VTE and MACE with JAK inhibitors (MHRA 2023).

points: **Eczema biologics/JAKi:** moderate–severe AE (e.g. EASI ≥16, DLQI ≥10) after at least one conventional systemic has failed or is unsuitable.

**Specialist screen before starting:** TB (IGRA ± CXR), hepatitis B/C, HIV, VZV serology, pregnancy, malignancy and demyelination history, vaccines up to date (give **live vaccines ≥4 weeks before** starting).
**During treatment:** infections, vaccines, surgery planning, pregnancy, new symptoms.

**Psoriasis:** avoid systemic steroids. Withdrawal can trigger **generalised pustular or erythrodermic psoriasis** (photo A06 shows localised pustular psoriasis; see the the [psoriasis](condition:psoriasis) notes).
**Record** the drug (hospital-only flag), the dose interval and the homecare provider; check interactions with every new prescription.

**Infection:** Lower threshold for review and antibiotics; **Hold the next dose during a significant infection** and contact the specialist team; Fever or serious infection → same-day assessment (presentations may be atypical)
**Pregnancy planning:** specialist advice. Many biologics can be continued; JAKi are contraindicated.
**Skin-cancer checks** (JAKi, TNF-i, previous PUVA or ciclosporin).

rungs.k: Methotrexate safety (IP level — the conventional systemic you are most likely to co-manage)
points: **Folic acid 5 mg once weekly** on a different day (some regimens use up to 6 days a week, never on the methotrexate day). It reduces GI, mucosal and hepatic toxicity.
**Dose in skin disease:** typically 7.5–25 mg once weekly, oral or subcutaneous; sometimes a 2.5–5 mg test dose first. Specialist-initiated.
Monitor BP and creatinine; stop or reduce if creatinine rises >25–30% from baseline.
Many CYP3A4 interactions (clarithromycin, azoles, grapefruit, St John's wort).
Gingival hyperplasia, hypertrichosis, tremor; hyperkalaemia (avoid potassium-sparing drugs).
persistent cough or breathlessness (MTX pneumonitis; infections on JAKi)
new IBD symptoms on an IL-17 inhibitor

items.t: Fever, sore throat, mouth ulcers or bruising on methotrexate: same-day FBC and stop until reviewed.
Never co-prescribe **trimethoprim or co-trimoxazole** with methotrexate.
Signs of serious infection or TB on a biologic or JAK inhibitor: urgent assessment and contact the specialist team.

pearls.t: "A red eye on dupilumab is ocular surface disease until proven otherwise, not just viral conjunctivitis — tell the dermatology team."
"IL-17 inhibitor + diarrhoea or bloody stool = IBD until proven otherwise."
"Methotrexate: one day a week, write the day down, no trimethoprim."
